reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, wide-packet re-review batch 6, 2026-08-01

samples_reviewed.question_text: Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend, are called ___.
Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend, are called ___.
Two intersecting lines that do NOT form a right angle are called ___.
Two lines that meet at a right angle (90°) are called ___.
Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend, are called ___.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: All three named line relationships appear at least once: parallel in seed 42's 'Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they extend', intersecting in seed 44, and perpendicular in seed 45's 'meet at a right angle (90°)', though 'draw' is never tested since all five items are definitional MCQs.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: While all three terms appear, coverage is skewed: parallel is tested in 3 of 5 seeds (42, 43, 46) versus one each for intersecting and perpendicular, and no sample asks the student to draw or identify lines from a diagram.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 44's correct answer, 'intersecting lines (not perpendicular)', bakes an unusual parenthetical qualifier into the answer text itself rather than using the clean term 'intersecting lines' a grade-3 student would actually select or write.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only three distinct question stems exist across five samples, with the parallel-lines question from seed 42 repeated verbatim in seeds 43 and 46 aside from option reordering.

competency_alignment.rationale: Unlike the sibling point/line/ray node, every named term here, parallel, intersecting, and perpendicular, does get exercised at least once, so the variation does build toward this competency's full stated scope even if unevenly.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: As a qualitative geometry competency there's no numeric ceiling at stake, and the 90° angle reference in seed 45 is standard, unembellished vocabulary for the grade.
